cut-every-treat.advice: Cut every treat until you are out of debt
cut-every-treat.line: Cutting every treat works for a few weeks when the month runs short. As the whole plan it makes people quit. Pick the few things you love, fund them on purpose, and cut the rest.

die-with-zero.advice: You can't take it with you: spend it and die with zero
die-with-zero.line: Die With Zero is a great book for people with more saved than they will ever spend. With a card at 25%, every dollar spent now costs a quarter more next year. Save it for Full Freedom.

every-dollar-to-retirement.advice: Every extra dollar goes into retirement accounts
every-dollar-to-retirement.line: Retirement is on track. A home, kids or travel come before 59 and a half, so this money needs to sit where you can reach it: sinking funds and a regular brokerage account.

frugal-is-freedom.advice: Squeeze every dollar: frugal is freedom
frugal-is-freedom.line: Living lean got you here. With the number banked, more cutting buys nothing. The new skill is spending on purpose, on the people and things you love.

give-when-rich.advice: Wait until you are rich to give
give-when-rich.line: Holding off made sense while the cards were growing. They are gone now. Giving a percent you pick, from money you have, does not put you at risk.

invest-every-spare-dollar.advice: Invest every spare dollar now: time in the market beats everything
invest-every-spare-dollar.line: Time in the market matters, once surprises stop landing on a card. While the month is going backwards, the next surprise eats the investment. Stop the bleeding first, then let compounding work.

max-the-401k-first.line: After the match, a Roth IRA and an HSA usually beat more 401(k): tax-free growth and more choice of funds. Maxing the 401(k) is the lever one step later, for Coast FI.

no-investing-until-debt-free.advice: Pay off every debt before you invest a dime
no-investing-until-debt-free.line: The match is a 50 to 100% return the day it lands. No card charges that much. Put in enough to get the whole match, even while you pay down the cards.

one-thousand-is-enough.advice: $1,000 is all the emergency fund you need
one-thousand-is-enough.line: $1,000 was the starter, and it did its job. With the high-interest debt gone, a job loss needs months, not a grand: your age divided by 5 months of spending.

pay-off-the-mortgage-first.advice: Pay off the mortgage early before you invest more
pay-off-the-mortgage-first.line: A low-rate mortgage is the last debt in the order. An extra dollar to it now is a dollar not compounding toward Coast FI. Pay it off at step 9, if at all.

renting-is-throwing-money-away.advice: Renting is throwing money away: buy as soon as you can
renting-is-throwing-money-away.line: Buying makes sense once the cards are gone, the job-loss fund is full and the down payment is saved. Before that, a house turns every repair into new debt.

save-a-thousand-first.line: You already have it. Now every spare dollar goes to the debt at 8% or more: cash past little e while a card grows is paying 25% to hold about 4%.

six-months-first.advice: Keep six months of expenses in cash before anything else
six-months-first.line: The big fund is step 4. For now, $1,000 (or your deductible, if it is smaller) keeps a flat tire off the card. The months of spending come after the match and the high-interest debt.

stay-until-the-number.advice: Never leave a steady job until everything is paid off and you hit your number
stay-until-the-number.line: That holds while the basics are open. At Coast FI, retirement takes care of itself, so the window for your own thing is open now. Waiting until you feel ready can mean missing it.
